channel.title: Articles by Emanuel Rusu, Shopify developer
channel.description: Guides to editing Shopify themes and notes from real Shopify projects.

item.title: Editing a Shopify theme, part 1: the theme editor, safely
item.description: There are four ways to change a Shopify theme, from clicking in the theme editor to a full Git workflow. Part 1 covers the one every store owner should master first, and the habit that makes all the others safe.

item.title: Editing a Shopify theme, part 2: the code editor in the admin
item.description: The quickest way into a theme's code needs nothing but a browser. Where to find it, what each folder does, a small section you can build in five minutes, and how to undo a file you broke.

item.title: Editing a Shopify theme, part 3: working locally with Shopify CLI
item.description: Shopify CLI gives you the theme on your own computer, your own editor and a live preview that reloads as you type. Installing it, the commands that matter, and the one mistake that wipes a merchant's changes.

item.title: Editing a Shopify theme, part 4: GitHub and a branch for every theme
item.description: Shopify's GitHub integration turns a branch into a theme and syncs both ways, including the merchant's edits. How to connect it, what it requires, and the branch setup I use so the live store only ever changes on purpose.

item.title: One jersey, one cart line: personalised shirts with a Cart Transform Function
item.description: A personalised hockey jersey is really four products: the shirt, the name, the number and the badges. Here is how I made them check out as one line for EV Zug without touching the price.

item.title: Moving a store's whole history without sending a single email
item.description: Importing tens of thousands of past customers and orders into a live Shopify store would normally email every one of them. Here is how I built a migration app where that cannot happen.

item.title: From 16.2 MB to 4.5 MB: slimming down a Shopify product page
item.description: A colour-variant product page on the new Curaprox store weighed 16.2 MB. Three unglamorous fixes brought it to 4.5 MB before launch. No framework changes, no new apps.

item.title: A football club's whole website on one Shopify theme
item.description: FC Basel runs its news, videos, league table, player pages and fan shop on a single Shopify theme. What it takes to make a store theme behave like a club website, and the jersey configurator in the middle of it.

item.title: Replacing Shopify search with Meilisearch: colours, markets and instant results
item.description: For Inuikii, I replaced Shopify's native search and collection filtering with a Meilisearch layer of about 3,000 lines. Why a footwear brand needs colour grouping, what market-aware prices mean for search, and the paid app that went away along the way.

item.title: When a credit check outage looks like a decline
item.description: On Ecofort, customers paying by invoice were being told no whenever the credit check provider had an outage. How I separated 'declined' from 'did not answer', and the performance pass that came with the same project.

item.title: A wishlist that survives the reload: server-side lists over a Shopify app proxy
item.description: Most theme wishlists live in the browser and vanish with it. For Chrüterhüsli I built one that is stored on the server through a Shopify app proxy, and a button that checks the server before it claims anything is saved.

item.title: Syncing content between Shopify stores: metaobjects, files and translations
item.description: Brands with several Shopify stores want to write content once. I worked on the internal app that syncs it: metaobjects whose definitions differ between stores, images that must survive the trip, and a file library too big to read in one go.

item.title: One allergen, three languages: filtering chocolate the way people search
item.description: Bruderer sells confectionery in German, English and French, with allergen data from several suppliers. Why the same allergen arrived under many spellings, and how a small normalisation step made the filters trustworthy.

item.title: Tabs that hide themselves: rebuilding a confectioner's design on Dawn
item.description: Confiserie Sprüngli wanted its existing design on Shopify's Dawn theme. The product page details that make that work, starting with information tabs that disappear when a product has nothing to put in them.

item.title: Six stores, one theme: loyalty points, currencies and structured data at Nile
item.description: Nile runs six Shopify stores, a test and a production store for each of CHF, EUR and GBP, from one shared theme. How a loyalty programme, country switching and SEO data work when every feature has to behave in three currencies.

item.title: Pricing a swim spa: installation choices as Shopify discounts
item.description: At Spa Solutions, the price of a swim spa depends on who installs it. As the sole developer, I built that choice into the product page and the cart with dynamic Shopify discounts and installation products that can never drift out of sync.

item.title: Faster football club stores without a rebuild: FC Zürich and FC St. Gallen
item.description: Two Swiss club stores, two kinds of speed. On FC Zürich, three days of work made collection and product pages at least 30% faster. On FC St. Gallen, a release-date filter that renders almost instantly by using CSS instead of reloading.

item.title: Pfand in the cart: a can deposit line for a German Shopify store
item.description: Drinks cans sold in Germany carry a deposit, and the cart has to charge it without confusing anyone. How I kept a deposit line in step with the cans on Glory Bomb, and why the cart count leaves it out.

item.title: PDF invoices from the Shopify customer account, built with jsPDF
item.description: For a Swiss car wash chain I made every order in the customer account downloadable as a proper invoice, with logo, VAT number and each discount listed. How it works in a Shopify theme, and the one-step card registration that came with it.

item.title: Hide a product's price with one tag in the Shopify admin
item.description: On Art of Fire the team hides the price of any product by adding a tag in the Shopify admin, with no code change. How tag-driven price visibility works in a theme, where it has to apply, and what it does not hide.
